title: Daily AI & Tech News Brief
summary: Concise AI, mobile, XR, and consumer technology news summaries with source links.

items.title: Microsoft details AutoJack attack against AI browsing agents
items.summary: Microsoft researchers described AutoJack, an exploit chain that can turn an AI browsing agent into a path for host code execution. The report says a malicious web page can use JavaScript to reach a privileged local service on the same machine, highlighting a security risk for agentic browsing systems.

items.title: Microsoft links Mastra AI supply-chain attack to North Korean hackers
items.summary: BleepingComputer reported that Microsoft attributed a Mastra AI supply-chain attack affecting more than 140 npm packages to Sapphire Sleet, also known as BlueNoroff. The attribution connects AI developer tooling risk with broader software supply-chain security concerns.

items.title: Apple smart-glasses timeline reportedly slips while Google glasses move toward fall shipping
items.summary: The Gadgeteer reported that Apple's smart-glasses plans have slipped toward late 2027, while Google's glasses are expected to ship this fall. The report is a third-party timeline claim, so it should be treated as unconfirmed until the companies announce product details directly.

items.title: Snap smart-glasses coverage highlights high-end AR hardware push
items.summary: Multiple outlets covered Snap's latest smart-glasses hardware, with reports citing pricing around the $2,000 range. The coverage shows continued industry experimentation with premium AR glasses even as mainstream adoption remains uncertain.

items.title: EssilorLuxottica and Applied Materials partner on smart-glasses optics
items.summary: Reports say EssilorLuxottica and Applied Materials are partnering on optics for smart glasses. The partnership points to continued investment in display and optical components that could shape future wearable-device designs.

items.title: WhatsApp tests animated message bubbles in iPhone beta
items.summary: The Tech Portal reported that WhatsApp added animated message bubbles in its latest iPhone beta version. The change is a consumer-facing interface experiment and may evolve before or if it reaches the stable app.

items.title: Google and Samsung system updates reported for Galaxy smartphones
items.summary: Zamin.uz reported that Google and Samsung released important system updates for Galaxy smartphones. The report frames the updates as part of ongoing platform maintenance for Android and Samsung devices.

items.title: AI music startup Tringbox raises seed funding
items.summary: Indian Startup News and other outlets reported that AI music startup Tringbox raised seed funding to expand its in-store music platform. The funding coverage shows continued investment interest in specialized AI tools for commercial audio and retail environments.

items.title: AI model providers expand tools for enterprise assistants
items.summary: Major AI platform providers continue to add workflow, retrieval, and safety controls for enterprise assistants. The updates are aimed at helping teams connect models to business data while keeping deployment and governance requirements visible.

items.title: Smartphone makers emphasize on-device AI features
items.summary: Recent mobile announcements show manufacturers positioning on-device AI as a core phone feature. Camera editing, translation, summarization, and personal assistant capabilities remain the most common consumer-facing examples.

items.title: XR hardware updates focus on lighter designs and clearer displays
items.summary: Consumer XR coverage continues to highlight lighter headset and smart glasses designs. Display clarity, battery life, and app ecosystems remain key factors for broader adoption.

items.title: Consumer technology firms continue privacy-focused feature updates
items.summary: Technology companies are continuing to market privacy controls as part of mainstream product updates. Recent messaging often focuses on account security, device-level protections, and clearer data controls for users.
